title: feat(mcp): the open draft door's registry and read tools, served where the token has metadata:write and the user holds manage_metadata
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBLW6dHPW6sSheA32XPKZzPV)_

Part of #34766 (PR-a: the registry, its admission and the three read tools; PR-b brings the save and discard tools, the verdict on each save and on `list_drafts`, and the app-crm end-to-end, and completes the card).

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:自托管运行时的 MCP 入口新增三个只读工具(`list_metadata_items`、`get_metadata_item`、`list_drafts`),让 AI 客户端能查看元数据和待发布草稿;本 PR 不写入任何东西。
- 为什么改:目前自托管应用上的 AI 客户端只能读写数据、完全无法参与搭建;这是"草稿门"的前半段,后半段(保存/丢弃草稿并当场返回发布裁决)在下一个 PR。
- 风险与回滚:只有令牌带 `metadata:write` 且该用户本人持有 `manage_metadata` 时才出现这些工具,任一不满足或权限读不到都不提供;读取结果与 `/meta` 接口对同一个人的裁决一致(缺少所需权限的仪表板/视图/应用、不在受众内的文档会被拒绝),在条目与列表闸门之前,两个读取工具还先过与 `/meta` 相同的类型级读取准入,调用者无权读取的元数据类型直接拒绝;持有 `manage_metadata` 也不例外;`type` 写成复数或别名(如 `dashboards`、`docs`)时先在入口折叠成单数再交给闸门,不能绕过;回滚即 revert 本 PR,不涉及数据变更。
- 先看:`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-authoring.ts` 的 `resolveHumanReader`(准入、用本人权限构造读取方、失败即关闭)与 `get_metadata_item` / `list_metadata_items` 里的类型级准入(`typeReadRefusal`)和两道读取闸门;`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` 的注入那几行;`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-authoring.test.ts` 的四个准入格。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --project local src/domains/mcp-authoring.test.ts`,预期 22 个测试全部通过。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

- **New `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-authoring.ts`**: the open `McpAuthoringToolRegistry` for the self-hosted MCP door (design `docs/design/mcp-local-first-door.md`, Design A). Three read tools over the metadata protocol's public reads:
  - `list_metadata_items({ type, state? })` over `getMetaItems` (draft-first: a pending draft is listed in place of its published version and marked `draft: true`; `state` selects `active` or `draft` only). An undeclared type is refused `400 INVALID_REQUEST` through the same `refuseUnknownMetaListType` the `/meta` list uses.
  - `get_metadata_item({ type, name, state? })` over `getMetaItem` (draft in place of the published version by default; a missing item answers `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`).
  - `list_drafts({ package? })` over `listDrafts` (no verdicts yet; the description promises none).
- **`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`**: resolves the injection per request and passes it to `handleHttpRequest` as `authoring`.
- **The `/meta` read gates, with the human as the caller (review M1)**: the door is not whole-for-author. `get_metadata_item` judges the item through `createMetaItemReadGate` and `list_metadata_items` judges the list through `createMetaListReadGate`, both exported by `@objectstack/rest` (already a dependency of the runtime, no cycle, nothing in `@objectstack/rest` edited). The caller the gates read is built from the human's own grants, the same resolution the admission does (`positions`, `permissions`, `permissionSetAddresses`, `systemPermissions`), never from the agent envelope. So a dashboard, a list view or an app whose `requiredPermissions` the human lacks, and a book or doc outside their ADR-0046 audience, are refused (`403 PERMISSION_DENIED`) or left out of the list, as every `/meta` door does for that human, `manage_metadata` or not (ruling 5856774816). The item read runs `STORED_VERSION_DOOR_POLICY`, the policy of the `/meta` doors that serve a stored version for authoring (the plain read's `?state=draft` branch among them): the per-caller gates, and the author exemption for a container's entries only, because this caller may save the item; a whole refusal stays a refusal. An `absent` verdict answers the door's own not-found. A gate that cannot evaluate refuses (a books read that throws answers `500`, never the doc), and a registry handed no gate reads nothing.
- **One fold at the door's boundary (review M1-b)**: the protocol's reads fold `type` (`dashboards` reads the dashboard, `canonicalizeMetaRequestType` over `canonicalMetaUrlType`), while both read gates judge the singular type only and leave the fold to their caller, as every `/meta` caller of them folds first. The door now folds the `type` argument once, with `canonicalMetaUrlType` from `@objectstack/spec/shared` (the protocol's own fold), in one module helper `canonicalTypeOf`, and hands the folded type to the protocol read, to `refuseUnknownMetaListType` and to both gate factories. So `get_metadata_item({ type: "dashboards" })` and `{ type: "docs" }` are judged as the dashboard and the doc they read, and `list_metadata_items({ type: "docs" })` drops what the gate drops. A name the fold answers no string for (an inherited member such as `constructor`, see Acceptance notes) stays the string the agent sent, the spelling every `/meta` door hands the protocol for it. The module header now says the gates apply whatever spelling is sent. PR-b's own local `canonicalTypeOf` is the same helper by name and signature, so the two collapse into this one.
- **The `/meta` type-level read admission (review M1-c)**: the MCP read tools run the same type-level read admission as `/meta` (`metaTypeReadRefusal`, exported by `@objectstack/rest`) before the item and list gates and before any protocol read, on the folded type, with the same human caller, on every `state` branch. A type the caller may not read is refused, as every `/meta` read refuses it, whether or not the named item exists. The module header and the changeset say so.
- **`list_drafts` runs no item gate**: `/meta/_drafts` runs none for this same caller (admitted by `mayReadPendingDrafts` alone), and a draft row carries the item's identity and its own `label`, no body for a gate to judge.
- **`list_metadata_items` with `state: "draft"` (review S1)**: kept on the draft-overlaid `getMetaItems` read and filtered to drafts, not moved to `listDrafts({ type })`, because the list gate judges each item's body (its `requiredPermissions`, a doc's audience) and a draft row carries none. The reason is in a code comment at the read.
- **Admission (seat ruling D1 A)**: the effective right is the intersection. The token consents (`metadata:write`; the MCP runtime's `grantsAuthoringTools` stays the authority on this half, it is read here only so an API key or a session costs no grant read), AND the human the token was issued to holds the capability: `resolveUserAuthzGrants` on `principal.userId` in the token's bound organization, judged by `metaWriteCapabilityVerdict` (operation `save`), never the agent envelope's own permissions (an OAuth agent carries none without `actions:execute`).
- **Fail closed**: no `userId` means no injection at all; a grant resolution that throws (or no data engine) yields a registry that lists nothing and refuses every call, plus one `warn`.
- **Listing rule (the #28938 shape)**: listing and calling read one verdict. A user without `manage_metadata` is listed none of the three tools; a call that reaches the registry anyway is refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`. A call stamped with a different user than the one admitted is refused the same way.
- **Host injection**: there is no host hook to defer to. A host with its own build door passes its own `authoring` at its own `handleHttpRequest` call; the option is one object, so the two registries never merge and their names never meet (stated in the module header).
- **`walledCatalogWriteVerdict`** is not applied here: it gates metadata writes and no `/meta` read. It joins with the save tool in PR-b.
- **Names (seat ruling D3 A)**: `list_metadata_items` / `get_metadata_item`, because `list_metadata` is a hosted platform tool (`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts:97`). None of the three is an MCP native tool (pinned in `packages/mcp/src/skill-md-surface-guard.test.ts`; the SDK throws on a duplicate registration).
- **`docs/design/mcp-local-first-door.md`**: one add-only dated note beside the tool table recording the rename. No other word changed.
- **`initialize` instructions / skill-md**: unchanged. Nothing in this PR is true yet that the design assigns to those surfaces for this door (no save, no verdict), so nothing is promised there.
- **Changeset** `.changeset/34766-mcp-open-draft-door-read.md`: `@objectstack/runtime` patch, with both declaration lines.

## Why

On a self-hosted app an AI client can read and write records over MCP and cannot build at all. The ruled design gives it a thin entry where it saves drafts and a person publishes them in Studio. This PR lands the entry's admission and its read half, so the write half (PR-b) only adds tools behind an already-pinned gate.

## Tests

Pins in `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-authoring.test.ts` (22 tests):

- the four D1 cells the seat requires: a token without `metadata:write` (no registry, the user's grant is never read); `metadata:write` with a user lacking `manage_metadata` (no tool listed, call refused 403 before any read); both present (the three tools listed and a read served); an API key (no registry);
- fail closed: an envelope with no user (nothing injected, no grant read); a grant resolution that throws (no tool listed, call refused, the request still served); a call stamped with another user;
- the read tools' behaviours (state selection, unknown type, 404, the package filter, coded refusals kept and uncoded throws answered without their text) and the name pin against the hosted platform tools;
- the `/meta` read gates through the real domain, with an envelope that carries no system permission: a dashboard whose `requiredPermissions` the human lacks is refused 403 and not listed, while one requiring a capability only the human holds (`manage_users`) is served (the allowed control, and proof the gate read the human); a doc outside the human's audience is refused 403 and not listed, while an `org` doc is served; a books read that throws serves no doc; a registry handed no gate reads nothing;
- the type-level read admission (review M1-c): a type the caller may not read is refused on item and list reads, on every state, before any protocol read (plural spelling and an absent name included), and a caller who holds what the type requires is served the same reads (the allowed control);
- the fold (review M1-b), against a protocol double whose reads fold `type` as the real protocol's do: `dashboards` and `docs` are refused 403 on the item read (no body, no `requiredPermissions` value in the refusal) and left out of the list, while `dashboards` / `people_board` is served as `type: "dashboard"`; the protocol is handed `doc` and `dashboard`, never the plural; and an inherited member's name (`constructor`, `toString`) reaches the protocol as the string sent.

`packages/mcp/src/skill-md-surface-guard.test.ts`: the three names collide with no native tool under every scope, and register beside the full native surface.

<details><summary>Ablations (each landed and restored by scripts/ablation-replace.mjs)</summary>

The suite imports the module relatively from `src/`, so no `dist/` sits on the path. Each mutation was proved on disk (anchor 1 to 0, blob changed) and each restore proved by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

Admission and fail-closed (round 1, on the module before a40a48ebbf, which changed only refusal codes):

1. Drop the user-grant check: `.allowed;` to `.allowed || true;` turns red exactly "a metadata:write token whose user lacks manage_metadata lists no tool, and a call is refused 403 before any read" (1 failed / 13 passed).
2. Drop fail-closed on a throwing resolution: `throw error;` at the top of the catch turns red exactly "a grant resolution that throws admits nothing: ..." (1 failed / 13 passed).
3. Drop fail-closed on no user: `if (!userId && false)` turns red exactly "an envelope with no user is injected nothing, and no grant is read" (1 failed / 13 passed).

The read gates (this round, at 2ef0ca896e, blob ddb16de3ac43):

4. Drop the item gate (the verdict becomes `serve` of the stored item): red are the dashboard pin, the doc pin and the books-read-throws pin (3 failed / 15 passed).
5. Drop the list gate (identity over the listed items): red are the dashboard pin and the doc pin at their list halves (2 failed / 16 passed).
6. Build the caller with the envelope's empty `systemPermissions` instead of the human's: red is the dashboard pin, whose allowed control (`manage_users`, held by the human only) is then refused (1 failed / 17 passed).

The fold (fix round for M1-b, at b7838f512f, blob a121757d6324):

7. Drop the fold (`return typeof folded === 'string' ? folded : type;` to `return type;`): red are exactly "a plural spelling is folded at the door ..." (`dashboards: expected false to be true`, i.e. the dashboard the human lacks the capability for was served) and "the door hands the protocol the folded type ..." (2 failed / 19 passed). Mutation landed anchor 1 to 0, blob a121757d6324 to 99e31994d616; restored blob == HEAD a121757d6324, `git diff HEAD` empty.

The type-level read admission (fix round for M1-c, at c50358b59c, blob 31253aca9077):

8. Drop the admission (`return refusal ? refuse(refusal.code, refusal.message, refusal.status) : undefined;` to `return refusal ? undefined : undefined;`): red is exactly "a type the caller may not read is refused on item and list reads, on every state, before any protocol read" (1 failed / 21 passed). Mutation landed anchor 1 to 0, blob 31253aca9077 to 2d4d2d940249; restored blob == HEAD 31253aca9077, `git diff HEAD` empty.
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- `@objectstack/runtime` typecheck at c50358b59c: exit 0. At b7838f512f (after building the runtime's dependency closure, `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/runtime^...' build`, exit 0): exit 0, `check:test-typecheck: OK` (27 files / 183 errors / 66 signatures held in the ledger, none new).
- Upstream of the fold, not changed here: `canonicalMetaUrlType` and `unrecognisedMetaTypeRefusal` (`packages/spec/src/meta-spelling/metadata-url-spelling.ts`) read `META_URL_TO_SINGULAR`, a plain frozen object, by bracket and by `in`, so an inherited member's name counts as a recognised spelling and folds to a non-string (`canonicalMetaUrlType('constructor')` answers the `Object` function, measured against the built spec). The door keeps the agent's string in that case and so behaves as before the fold; what a public `/meta` door answers for such a segment was not measured, so this is a note, not a card.
- `@objectstack/mcp` `check:test-typecheck`: OK (round 1; this round changes nothing in `packages/mcp`).

- `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`: one line, `'mcp-authoring.ts': { handBuilt: 0 },` in `DISPATCHER_DOMAINS`. Reason, in the gate's own words: "packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-authoring.ts NOT DECLARED. Add it to DISPATCHER_DOMAINS in scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs. A domain that answers only through the `deps.*` helpers declares { handBuilt: 0 }". The module builds MCP tool results and no REST body. Approved by the dispatching seat (option A). No other change to that file; no test reads its table, and its own `--self-test` passes.
